answer: A single karst checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Forging 82 aliases thus costs 446 bonds held for 17 days each, plus the anchor attestations those aliases can never earn. Each identity must lock a bond, called a nebula, before it can post or attest. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an attacker cannot recover it by rotating identities. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
